newsitem.title: USA: Georgia jobless rate steady at 4.5 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Georgia jobless rate steady at 4.5 pct in Sept.

text.p: Georgia's unemployement rate was 4.5 percent for September, unchanged from August and down from 5.1 percent a year ago, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said Monday.
"As we expected, the closing of the Summer Olympics didn't have a negative impact on the state's unemployment rate," Poythress said.
For the 20-county metropolitan Atlanta area, the unemployment rate rose slightly to 3.8 in September from 3.7 percent in August, but down from 4.4 percent a year ago.

"We have shown some job loss since the Olympics but we knew that would happen because the jobs were temporary to begin with," Poythress said. "What is encouraging is that our economy is strong enough to absorb the Olympic job losss without a resulting rate increase."

Georgia has lost 42,000 temporary jobs since July, mostly in the trade and service-related industries connected to the Olympics. But the state gained 99,900 jobs over the year, putting total employment at 3.77 million in September.
The employment total hit a record high 3.8 million during the Olympics in July.
